# Missingness panel data ELCA

library (naniar)
library (tidyverse)

library (haven)

library (janitor)

library (assertthat)
library (purrr)
```

Preparing workspace and opening up our databases database

setwd("C:/Users/Daniela/OneDrive/Documentos/UvT/Second year/Thesis/Data bases")

source ("code_FULL_panel.R")

```

Taking into account we want to assess for attrition between our databases, a variable that has no missingness within out full panel data will be chosen to be able to generate a dummy that works as a filter.

```{r}


sum(is.na (short_panel_2010$sexo))

sum(is.na(partial_panel$sexo))

sum(is.na (full_panel$sexo))
```

### 2010 vs. 2013

Wrangling our dataset through left_join instead of inner_join to keep observations from 2010 that no longer appear in 2013, checking for duplicates and proceeding with elimination after manual examination

```{r}
identifiers_2010 <- short_panel_2010 %>%
  select(consecutivo, llave_ID_lb,orden, sexo, etnia, estrato_2010)

#changing name of sex variable to be able to identify missingness later on
miss.short_panel_2013 <- rename (short_panel_2013, 
                                 miss_2013 = sexo)

data2013 <- left_join(
  identifiers_2010,
  miss.short_panel_2013,
  by = c("consecutivo", "llave_ID_lb", "orden"))


```

### Dataset wrangling

Wrangling our dataset through left_join instead of inner_join to keep observations from 2013 that no longer appear in 2016, checking for duplicates and proceeding with elimination after manual examination

```{r}
identifiers_2013 <- data2013 %>%
  select(consecutivo, llave_ID_lb,orden, sexo, etnia, estrato_2010, miss_2013, estrato_2013)

#changing name of sex variable to be able to identify missingness later on
miss.short_panel_2016 <- rename (short_panel_2016, 
                                 miss_2016 = sexo)

full_data<- left_join(
  identifiers_2013,
  miss.short_panel_2016,
  by = c("consecutivo", "llave_ID_lb", "orden"))




```

## Missingness analyses

### Full attrition

Comparing across years the amount of people lost in total.

```{r}

#obtaining frquency table from 2010
attrition2010 <- full_data %>% 
  summarise(N = sum(!is.na (sexo)), 
    Missing = sum(is.na (sexo))) %>%
  mutate(
    "% Missing Data" = round(100 * Missing / sum(c(N,Missing)), 2)) %>% 
  mutate(
    Year = "2010",
    .before = 1
  )

#obtaining frequency table from 2013
attrition2013 <- full_data %>% 
  summarise(
    N = sum(!is.na (miss_2013)), 
    Missing = sum(is.na (miss_2013))) %>%
  mutate(
    "% Missing Data" = round(100 * Missing / sum(c(N,Missing)), 2)) %>% 
  mutate(
    Year = "2013",
    .before = 1
  )

#obtaining frequency table from 2016
attrition2016 <- full_data %>% 
  summarise(
    N = sum(!is.na (miss_2016)), 
    Missing = sum(is.na (miss_2016))) %>%
  mutate(
    "% Missing Data" = round(100 * Missing / sum(c(N,Missing)), 2)) %>% 
  mutate(
    Year = "2016",
    .before = 1
  )



#generating conjunct frequency tables

#2010 vs. 2013
attrition2010_2013 <- rbind (attrition2010, attrition2013)

#Full attrition 
full_attrition <- rbind(attrition2010_2013, attrition2016)
full_attrition



```

**Total cases lost across waves: 1833**

## Missingness by demographic variables

To assess for patterns in the data that may be related to vulnerability factors, we will look into the missingness across the demographic variables through frequency tables and graphical aid

### Sex

Frequency tables

```{r}
sex.attrition2010 <- full_data %>% 
  mutate (Sex = sexo) %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>% 
  summarise(
    Observed = sum(!is.na (sexo)), 
    Missing = sum(is.na (sexo)), 
    Total = n()) %>%
  mutate(
    "% Missing Within" = round(100 * Missing / Total, 2), 
    "% Missing Between" = round(100 * Missing / sum(c(Observed,Missing)), 2)) %>% 
  mutate(
    Year = "2010",
    .before = 1
  )

sex.attrition2013 <- full_data %>% 
  mutate (Sex = sexo) %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>% 
  summarise(
    Observed = sum(!is.na (miss_2013)), 
    Missing = sum(is.na (miss_2013)), 
    Total = n()) %>%
  mutate(
    "% Missing Within" = round(100 * Missing / Total, 2), 
    "% Missing Between" = round(100 * Missing / sum(c(Observed,Missing)), 2)) %>% 
  mutate(
    Year = "2013",
    .before = 1
  )



sex.attrition2016 <- full_data %>% 
  mutate (Sex = sexo) %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>% 
  summarise(
    Observed = sum(!is.na (miss_2016)), 
    Missing = sum(is.na (miss_2016)),
    Total = n()) %>%
  mutate(
    "% Missing Within" = round(100 * Missing / Total, 2), 
    "% Missing Between" = round(100 * Missing / sum(c(Observed,Missing)), 2)) %>% 
  mutate(
    Year = "2016",
    .before = 1
  )



sex.attrition2010_2013 <- rbind (sex.attrition2010, sex.attrition2013)
full.sex.attrition <- rbind (sex.attrition2010_2013, sex.attrition2016)
full.sex.attrition
```

#### Graph

```{r}

full.sex.attrition.long <- full.sex.attrition %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Observed, Missing),
    names_to = "Data",
    values_to = "N"
  )

ggplot(full.sex.attrition.long, aes(x = Sex, y = N, fill=Data)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ Year) +
  labs(
    title = "Missingness distribution by sex",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "N",
    fill="Data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

### Socioeconomic Stratum

    .before = 1
  )

ses.attrition2016 <- full_data %>% 
   mutate (SES = estrato_2010, 
          Sex = sexo) %>%
  group_by(SES, Sex) %>% 
  summarise(
    Observed = sum(!is.na (miss_2016)), 
    Missing = sum(is.na (miss_2016)), 
    Total = n()) %>%

ses.attrition2010_2013 <- rbind (ses.attrition2010, ses.attrition2013)

write.csv(full.ses.attrition, "full_ses_attrition.csv")
